39:41.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لِلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ فَمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ فَلِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن ضَلَّ فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيۡهَاۖ وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيۡهِم بِوَكِيلٍ
39:41.en: Lo! We have revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture for mankind with truth. Then whosoever goeth right it is for his soul, and whosoever strayeth, strayeth only to its hurt. And thou art not a warder over them

39:42.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلۡأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوۡتِهَا وَٱلَّتِي لَمۡ تَمُتۡ فِي مَنَامِهَاۖ فَيُمۡسِكُ ٱلَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَيُرۡسِلُ ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمًّىۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
39:42.en: Allah receiveth (men's) souls at the time of their death, and that (soul) which dieth not (yet) in its sleep. He keepeth that (soul) for which He hath ordained death and dismisseth the rest till an appointed term. Lo! herein verily are portents for people who take thought

39:43.ar: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُفَعَآءَۚ قُلۡ أَوَلَوۡ كَانُواْ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
39:43.en: Or choose they intercessors other than Allah? Say: What! Even though they have power over nothing and have no intelligence

39:44.ar: قُل لِّلَّهِ ٱلشَّفَٰعَةُ جَمِيعࣰ اۖ لَّهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
39:44.en: Say: Unto Allah belongeth all intercession. His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth. And afterward unto Him ye will be brought back

39:45.ar: وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَحۡدَهُ ٱشۡمَأَزَّتۡ قُلُوبُ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِذَا هُمۡ يَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ
39:45.en: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who believe not in the Hereafter are repelled, and when those (whom they worship) beside Him are mentioned, behold! they are glad

39:46.ar: قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ عَٰلِمَ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَٱلشَّهَٰدَةِ أَنتَ تَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَ عِبَادِكَ فِي مَا كَانُواْ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَ
39:46.en: Say: O Allah! Creator of the heavens and the earth! Knower of the Invisible and the Visible! Thou wilt judge between Thy slaves concerning that wherein they used to differ

112:1.en: Say: He is Allah, the One

2:136.ar: قُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ ٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
2:136.en: Say (O Muslims): We believe in Allah and that which is revealed unto us and that which was revealed unto Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and that which Moses and Jesus received, and that which the prophets received from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and unto Him we have surrendered

3:84.ar: قُلۡ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
3:84.en: Say (O Muhammad): We believe in Allah and that which is revealed unto us and that which was revealed unto Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and that which was vouchsafed unto Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and unto Him we have surrendered

3:85.ar: وَمَن يَبۡتَغِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡإِسۡلَٰمِ دِينࣰ ا فَلَن يُقۡبَلَ مِنۡهُ وَهُوَ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
3:85.en: And whoso seeketh as religion other than the Surrender (to Allah) it will not be accepted from him, and he will be a loser in the Hereafter

35:18.ar: وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةࣱ وِزۡرَ أُخۡرَىٰۚ وَإِن تَدۡعُ مُثۡقَلَةٌ إِلَىٰ حِمۡلِهَا لَا يُحۡمَلۡ مِنۡهُ شَيۡءࣱ وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰٓۗ إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَمَن تَزَكَّىٰ فَإِنَّمَا يَتَزَكَّىٰ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
35:18.en: And no burdened soul can bear another's burden, and if one heavy laden crieth for (help with) his load, naught of it will be lifted even though he (unto whom he crieth) be of kin. Thou warnest only those who fear their Lord in secret, and have established worship. He who groweth (in goodness), groweth only for himself, (he cannot by his merit redeem others). Unto Allah is the journeying

110:2.ar: وَرَأَيۡتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدۡخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفۡوَاجࣰ ا
110:2.en: And thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops

17:85.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّي وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:85.en: They are asking thee concerning the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is by command of my Lord, and of knowledge ye have been vouchsafed but little

53:26.ar: ۞وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغۡنِي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن يَأۡذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرۡضَىٰٓ
53:26.en: And how many angels are in the heavens whose intercession availeth naught save after Allah giveth leave to whom He chooseth and accepteth

19:47.ar: قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكَۖ سَأَسۡتَغۡفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّيٓۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِي حَفِيࣰّ ا
19:47.en: He said: Peace be unto thee! I shall ask forgiveness of my Lord for thee. Lo! He was ever gracious unto me

9:114.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱسۡتِغۡفَارُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَن مَّوۡعِدَةࣲ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُۥٓ أَنَّهُۥ عَدُوࣱّ لِّلَّهِ تَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُۚ إِنَّ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لَأَوَّٰهٌ حَلِيمࣱ‏
9:114.en: The prayer of Abraham for the forgiveness of his father was only because of a promise he had promised him, but when it had become clear unto him that he (his father) was an enemy to Allah he (Abraham) disowned him. Lo! Abraham was soft of heart, long-suffering

9:55.ar: فَلَا تُعۡجِبۡكَ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُمۡۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُم بِهَا فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَتَزۡهَقَ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
9:55.en: So let not their riches nor their children please thee (O Muhammad). Allah thereby intendeth but to punish them in the life of the world and that their souls shall pass away while they are disbelievers

9:85.ar: وَلَا تُعۡجِبۡكَ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَأَوۡلَٰدُهُمۡۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُعَذِّبَهُم بِهَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَتَزۡهَقَ أَنفُسُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ كَٰفِرُونَ
9:85.en: Let not their wealth nor their children please thee! Allah purposeth only to punish them thereby in the world, and that their souls shall pass away while they are disbelievers

oNHV9lwI8M8.speaker: adnan
oNHV9lwI8M8.speaker_note: continues his weekly Arabic tafsir of Az-Zumar and cites an explanation from one of his own teachers
oNHV9lwI8M8.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:41-46)
oNHV9lwI8M8.one_line: Reasons to be sincere: Allah gains nothing from us, souls return to Him in sleep and death, and intercession belongs to Him alone.
oNHV9lwI8M8.summary: These verses give reasons to be sincere. The Book was sent down 'upon' the Prophet, meaning he too must live it, and whoever is guided benefits himself, because Allah gains nothing from us. Knowing He needs nothing makes sincerity easier: He offers lasting bliss, which humans have never achieved alone and are further from today despite technology, and gives us acts like prayer that bring us closest to it now, so offering them to anyone else is shameful. The Prophet is not their guardian, and dawah is not about numbers. Verse 42 distinguishes biological death from Allah's taking of the soul, as one of his teachers explained: in sleep the soul is taken and returned. No creature survives without sleep and science cannot fully say why, a daily sign that the soul needs Allah; since it returns to Him in sleep and death regardless, give Him your waking hours too. The alternative is taking intercessors without His leave, who own nothing and understand nothing; all intercession belongs to Allah, and even the Prophet will turn from those who changed his way. Those who reject the Hereafter recoil when Allah alone is mentioned, preferring connections who arrange things, but every person will stand before Him alone.

outline.heading: Opening
Sincerity: the greatest act of the heart
outline.gist: It is given half a juz in Az-Zumar and then distilled in Surat Al-Ikhlas.

outline.heading: Verse 41 recited
outline.gist: The Book sent down for people in truth; guidance and error each return to the person.

outline.heading: Sent down 'to you' and 'upon you'
outline.gist: 'To' means passing it on to others; 'upon' means you are the one meant to apply it.

outline.heading: Al-Baqarah and Aal-Imran compared
outline.gist: One says what was sent 'to' Ibrahim and his sons, the other 'upon' them, matching continuation of the message versus applying it.

outline.heading: The Prophet bound by the same demands
outline.gist: Allah addresses him so we know he is our model in obedience, not exempt; sent with truth means its basis and aim are truth.

outline.heading: Whoever is guided, it is for himself
outline.gist: Allah needs nothing from us; if He gained something the relationship would feel like an exchange.

outline.heading: Knowing He needs nothing eases sincerity
outline.gist: It is hard to be sincere where there is mutual benefit; working for reward is fine, but higher sincerity sees He offers everything and gains nothing.

outline.heading: Prayer: a connection that trains the self
outline.gist: Salah comes from silah, connection; prostration, seeking forgiveness and praise train the self, and the benefit is yours.

outline.heading: Lasting bliss we cannot reach alone
outline.gist: Humans keep failing to secure lasting happiness; with longer lives and more comfort, studies find people less happy than before.

outline.heading: No barakah in our time
outline.gist: Ten years ago people back home ended the day with tea and conversation; now the day vanishes in work.

outline.heading: Worship brings you closest to bliss now
outline.gist: Sincere worship, zuhd, prayer and love of Allah bring lasting bliss nearest in this life, as the scholar who said his garden was in his chest.

outline.heading: Deeds have worth only because He gave them worth
outline.gist: He values deeds that do not benefit Him and promises your goal for them; giving them to someone else makes no sense.

outline.heading: You are not their guardian
outline.gist: Error harms only the one who strays; the Prophet held himself responsible for others' guidance and was told he was not.

outline.heading: Dawah is not about numbers
outline.gist: We call people because we love Allah and want them to know Him; Surat An-Nasr ends with people entering the religion for their own sake.

outline.heading: Verse 42 recited
outline.gist: Allah takes souls at death and in sleep, keeps those decreed to die and returns the others.

outline.heading: Taking the soul versus death
outline.gist: Tawaffa adds receiving in full; the common use of 'mutawaffi' for the deceased is weak in Arabic.

outline.heading: His teacher's explanation
outline.gist: If tawaffa meant death the verse would be redundant; death is the body's end, tawaffa the soul's departure.

outline.heading: In sleep the soul is taken and returned
outline.gist: The soul is from Allah's command and little is known of it; the sleeper is alive biologically while Allah takes the soul.

outline.heading: The waking supplications
outline.gist: Praise to Allah who gave us life after death and returned my soul: the hadith link sleep with death.

outline.heading: A sign: no one can go without sleep
outline.gist: Even those with insomnia fall asleep; the brain must enter sleep states or the person dies.

outline.heading: Sleep deprivation as torture
outline.gist: An American inquiry into CIA torture omitted keeping prisoners under lights, which neuroscientists count among the worst methods.

outline.heading: Science cannot fully say why we sleep
outline.gist: The brain-reorganising theory is plausible but unproven after millions spent; all creatures sleep every day and we cannot say why.

outline.heading: The soul's absolute need for Allah
outline.gist: If the soul did not return to Him every few hours we would die; sleep guarantees the return whether you will it or not.

outline.heading: Give Him your waking hours too
outline.gist: Your soul returns to Him alone in sleep and death; why mix it with others while awake?

outline.heading: Verses 43-46 recited
outline.gist: Intercessors, hearts recoiling at Allah's name, and the call to the Originator; 'fatir' and 'alim' take the vocative form.

outline.heading: 'Or have they taken': a refused offer
outline.gist: 'Am' shows the previous verses offered something; refusing sincerity, the alternative is false intercessors.

outline.heading: What an intercessor is
outline.gist: One with standing before the powerful; intercession is real in Quran and Sunnah but never without Allah's permission.

outline.heading: Owning nothing and understanding nothing
outline.gist: The idolater's idea is that an intercessor forces the outcome; in tawhid Allah decides who is interceded for, as with Ibrahim and his father.

outline.heading: The Prophet turns from those who changed his way
outline.gist: At the Basin he calls 'my companions' and is told he does not know what they introduced after him.

outline.heading: All intercession belongs to Allah
outline.gist: To Him belong the heavens and earth and to Him you return; He wills the righteous to intercede for sinners.

outline.heading: Allah intercedes last
outline.gist: After prophets, angels and the righteous intercede, Allah brings out whoever has an atom's weight of good in his heart.

outline.heading: Why seek anyone else's approval?
outline.gist: The one whose opinion you courted cannot intercede without Allah's leave; do not be dazzled by people's wealth and power.

outline.heading: Hearts that recoil at Allah alone
outline.gist: Ishma'azza, used only here, is instinctive revulsion; those who deny the Hereafter recoil because tawhid means accountability.

outline.heading: Ahmed Deedat's reply
outline.gist: Paralysed but still answering by eye, he told a questioner his surprise at finding nothing would be less than the other's at finding something.

outline.heading: We prefer someone with connections
outline.gist: People want a lawyer who knows the judge; on the Day there is no side room for friends.

outline.heading: Originator of the heavens, Knower of all
outline.gist: Fatir means bringing into being from the start; He alone creates and knows and will judge their disputes.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance

themes.label: Modernity, secularism, materialism and their effects
themes.note: Technology has not brought happiness; time has lost its barakah.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: We are not guardians of people's guidance, and dawah is not about numbers.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Sleep shows the soul's constant need to return to Allah; give Him the waking hours as well.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Intercession exists only by Allah's permission; false intercessors own and understand nothing.

quran.point: Sincerity distilled in a short surah after Az-Zumar's long treatment
What was sent down 'to' Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq
What was sent down 'upon' them, followed by 'whoever seeks other than Islam'
Whoever purifies himself does so for his own good
Victory is people entering Allah's religion, not numbers for their own sake
The soul is of my Lord's command and you were given little knowledge
Angels' intercession avails nothing except after Allah's permission
Ibrahim promises to ask forgiveness for his father
Ibrahim disowned his father once he was clearly Allah's enemy
Let not their wealth and children impress you
The same warning repeated

hadith.gist: On waking: praise to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection
Praise to Allah who returned my soul to me and permitted me to remember Him
At the Basin some are driven away; the Prophet calls 'my companions' and is told he does not know what they introduced after him
Prophets, angels and the righteous intercede, then Allah brings out of the Fire whoever has an atom's weight of good

maxims: Sent 'to you' to convey, 'upon you' to apply
He gains nothing from you, so give it all to Him
Your soul returns to Him in sleep; give Him your waking hours
There is no side room for friends on the Day

stories.point: Distinguished death of the body from Allah's taking of the soul, which makes the verse coherent.

stories.who: A scholar imprisoned by his enemies
stories.point: His garden was in his chest; prison was seclusion, exile travel and killing martyrdom.
The denier's shock at finding a Hereafter will be greater than the believer's at finding none.

contemporary: Studies finding people less happy in the technological age despite longer lives
A US inquiry into CIA and Guantanamo torture that left out sleep deprivation under constant light
Ahmed Deedat's final years of dawah while paralysed
takeaways: Remember Allah gains nothing from your deeds, and offer them to Him alone
Treat prayer as connection and training of the self
Call people to Allah out of love, not to grow numbers
Use your waking hours to stay connected to Allah
Do not court people's approval or rely on connections for the Hereafter

62:1.ar: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ ٱلۡقُدُّوسِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
62:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, the Mighty, the Wise

59:23.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡمَلِكُ ٱلۡقُدُّوسُ ٱلسَّلَٰمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُ ٱلۡمُهَيۡمِنُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡجَبَّارُ ٱلۡمُتَكَبِّرُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
59:23.en: He is Allah, than Whom there is no other Allah, the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, Peace, the Keeper of Faith, the Guardian, the Majestic, the Compeller, the Superb. Glorified be Allah from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

59:24.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:24.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

VrpBqn7hw9A.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Jumuah, Part 1: Verse 1
VrpBqn7hw9A.one_line: Opening Surat Al-Jumuah, he argues Jumuah was designed as a weekly system of leadership that Muslims have neutralized, then reads 62:1's four names as qualities of leadership.
VrpBqn7hw9A.summary: Starting the surah, he spends most of the session on what Jumuah was meant to be. It is the most important prayer and was built on leadership, not scholarship: caliphs, governors and commanders gave the khutbah, and this weekly direction helped Islam spread across three continents within thirty years. Once the minbar went to hired mouthpieces, or to imams reading government papers, Jumuah was neutralized. In the West nothing stops Muslims from fixing this, so the person who actually leads a masjid should give the khutbah, or an imam whose vision the board truly follows; imams must also be held accountable. He suggests separate khutbahs in each community language instead of translation. Turning to 62:1, he explains that surahs opening with tasbih remind us of purpose before technical rulings, so the group never becomes the goal as the tribe was in the age of ignorance. The four names, King, Holy, Mighty and Wise, show why Allah deserves to be followed and model the qualities of a leader: ownership, higher purpose, strength and wisdom. Without them Muslims are a headless chicken, as Gaza exposed. He recalls how al-Andalus fell through disunity and calls for unity and a focus on basics such as youth, mental health and family over minor fiqh disputes.

outline.heading: Jumuah: the most important prayer
outline.gist: Of all the prayers Jumuah ranks first by a wide margin. It can only be prayed at a masjid, and a man who prays at home instead without excuse is held accountable.

outline.heading: What this juz organizes
outline.gist: The Madinan surahs of this juz organize relationships in the Muslim nation: spouses, family, leaders, citizenship, relations with non-Muslims and the social contract, with leadership built in through the ritual of Jumuah.

outline.heading: A universal weekly gathering
outline.gist: Wherever two or three Muslims live, from Alaska to a jungle, they build a masjid and someone stands to speak on Friday. Hundreds of millions attend every week, a system meant to guarantee leadership that Muslims have still managed to ruin.

outline.heading: Jumuah was built on leadership, not knowledge
outline.gist: The caliph, governor or commander gave the khutbah, and anyone else on the minbar spoke on the leadership's behalf. Allah gathers the people so that every week their leader addresses problems and sets the next step.

outline.heading: Leadership behind Islam's rapid spread
outline.gist: Within thirty years of the Prophet's death the caliphate was the largest power on earth, spanning three continents from Central Asia to the Horn of Africa, because a system of leadership was built into the religion.

outline.heading: Jumuah began in Medina, once there was a state
outline.gist: Jumuah was never held in Mecca. It was revealed early in Medina once the Prophet had his own city, and those who gave it were the men he sent to lead armies, judge or govern.

outline.heading: A minbar with no authority
outline.gist: Once the speaker has no pull, reading a paper handed to him or hired as a mouthpiece, Jumuah is neutralized and people gradually stop feeling its importance.

outline.heading: One Jumuah per city in classical fiqh
outline.gist: In the Shafi'i view a city holds one Jumuah, so where several are held people pray Dhuhr afterwards; other imams allow several when there is need. He offers it as food for thought, not a ruling.

outline.heading: Seventeen years before he gave a khutbah
outline.gist: With about 25 Jumuahs in London anyone with a beard and a hat can speak, yet he studied seventeen years before his teachers let him give khutbahs in their presence, then three more before giving them out of need, and he would sit down if scholars were present.

outline.heading: The community's real leader belongs on the minbar
outline.gist: Most masajid hire imams to get things done, not to be followed for their vision, so the person actually leading, usually the board chair, should give the khutbah. A leader needs no scholarly permission and can be taught the basics.

outline.heading: A scholar may speak for a leader only as his adviser
outline.gist: A leader who cannot learn to give a khutbah should not lead. A scholar may speak on his behalf only as a trusted adviser whose counsel is sought, not as a paid or frightened voice.

outline.heading: A shy caliph who still gave the khutbahs
outline.gist: Even a famously shy, soft-voiced companion who was no public speaker gave every khutbah his role required, with Ali helping train him, because leading means speaking.

outline.heading: Censored imams abroad, nothing missing here but understanding
outline.gist: He disclaims any wish to lead. Tyrant governments fax imams their khutbahs on Thursday night, but in the West nobody dictates the topic; what is missing is understanding, so future board members should hire imams only as leaders they will follow.

outline.heading: The khutbah belongs to whoever is accountable
outline.gist: A hired imam can lead the five prayers, but the khutbah should come from the person who makes decisions and answers for failures. When the 36,000 Muslims of London suffer, even when Muslims are run down at a street light, nobody can be held to account.

outline.heading: Imams must be held accountable too
outline.gist: Unpaid, he speaks freely while other imams are censored by their boards, yet imams make mistakes, and a speaker everyone applauds stops researching. Rules exist to protect people from themselves, and this surah organizes leadership through Jumuah.

outline.heading: Every Friday since the first
outline.gist: Muslims have not missed a Friday since the first one, even through COVID. Fifty Jumuahs a year make 500 compulsory half-hour lectures a decade, and wasting them pains him deeply.

outline.heading: Masajid led by people who set the vision
outline.gist: The masajid of his youth were led by pharmacists, physicians and business owners who made the decisions and set the direction, and they thrived. He does not care who leads, only that the leader comes forward, with any other speaker aligned to his vision.

outline.heading: Why the next generation may stop coming
outline.gist: Crowded Friday prayers breed false confidence: if people learn nothing and see no progress, the second or third generation will drift away.

outline.heading: Standing where the Prophet would stand
outline.gist: Without benefit Jumuah could empty like other faiths' houses of worship. Allah summons the people, so the khateeb needs a message worth hearing and should speak as the Prophet, whose place he fills, would have wanted.

outline.heading: Attend to learn, and a friend's hard question
outline.gist: An attendee comes intending to learn and looks for something good even in a weak khutbah. Still, a friend once asked why Allah would hold him accountable for missing what they had just heard, a sign the system needs adjusting.

outline.heading: Separate Jumuahs for each language
outline.gist: Bilingual khutbahs never work because a real idea needs 20 to 30 minutes in one language. He proposes separate Jumuahs in Arabic, English, Urdu, Bangla and Somali, since everyone has a right to hear Allah's message in their mother tongue.

outline.heading: Jumuah as a weekly tool for direction
outline.gist: A compulsory gathering every seven days could put everyone on the same page and mobilize them, but while every group does its own thing and speakers only tell stories, nothing changes.

outline.heading: Tasbih openings: remember why before the rulings
outline.gist: Surahs that open with tasbih precede technical, practical material with a reminder of purpose. Leadership and community matter because Allah wants them, so Jumuah must be run the way He wants, not the way that suits an organization.

outline.heading: When the purpose is forgotten, the means take its place
outline.gist: Many surahs of this technical juz open this way because once the purpose is forgotten, the means or the group become the purpose and sincerity is ruined.

outline.heading: Loyalty for Allah's sake, not tribal loyalty
outline.gist: Muslims value their group only because Allah commands it; otherwise it is nationalism, the tribalism of the age of ignorance captured by the poet who follows his tribe whether it errs or is guided. He then renders the verse: all in the heavens and earth exalts Allah.

outline.heading: Al-Malik: He owns it all
outline.gist: The four names explain why Allah is worthy of being followed. As King all sovereignty is His and we are His property, so there is no point turning to anyone else.

outline.heading: Al-Quddus: claiming no flaw in Him
outline.gist: Tasbih means attributing no flaw or mistake to Allah; what we dislike we accept, assuming we do not yet understand it. This way of speaking about and to Allah sets Muslims apart even from other believers in God.

outline.heading: Allah makes His case for being followed
outline.gist: Though He has no need to, Allah describes Himself so that we follow Him with understanding rather than blindly: He owns all and makes no mistakes.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz: beyond comprehension and unbeatable
outline.gist: Al-Aziz carries two senses: one whose knowledge is far beyond ours, and one who cannot be overcome.

outline.heading: Al-Hakim: He commands only what serves you
outline.gist: One so powerful and beyond blame might seem free to command anything; as the All-Wise He only commands what is in our interest. The only similar grouping of names closes Al-Hashr.

outline.heading: The names as a leader's pillars: a purpose above self
outline.gist: The four names are also the pillars of a good leader. Holiness means leading for a higher purpose and the good of all, not for status, power, fame or votes.

outline.heading: Ownership: Umar and the unpaved road
outline.gist: Umar worried that Allah would ask him about a sheep stumbling on a road he had not paved. Leaders who feel no responsibility, or let others suffer while they prosper, are not leaders; Allah uses words we understand without being like a human leader.

outline.heading: Strength and wisdom, or a headless chicken
outline.gist: A leader must be strong and never back down, and wise, since good intentions without wisdom run people into a brick wall. He once thought of bringing his son's headless toy chicken to Jumuah as a picture of the community.

outline.heading: Gaza: a brief taste of shared leadership
outline.gist: These 107 days have been the worst since the Syria bombings of 2015, yet for 45 to 50 days communities turned to NCCM and Hikma for next steps and it felt like direction. Then it faded, leaving masajid unable to advocate or reach those with political influence.

outline.heading: Small groups too proud to work together
outline.gist: Stubbornness, arrogance and labelling others deviant keep groups apart, as if one small masjid in a corner of the world matters on its own; its only value is in being part of something larger.

outline.heading: Al-Andalus: fiqh and science grown in a new culture
outline.gist: Al-Andalus showed Europe religion and science together. Its Maliki and other scholars, some of whom invented instruments, developed fiqh suited to a new place, as fiqh should grow with time and setting.

outline.heading: Why al-Andalus fell
outline.gist: Its fall brought gruesome torture, and it fell because some fifty petty kingdoms each wanted independence, so they were picked off like dominoes.

outline.heading: No luxury of debating details
outline.gist: Early Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i and Hanbali scholars could debate fine points of prayer because Muslims were strong and united; today we are too weak to argue over small fiqh issues.

outline.heading: Focus on the basics, starting with Jumuah
outline.gist: Run Jumuah well and give people every reason to come, spiritually, socially and practically; if we cannot get the first ritual right, arguing over tertiary issues is pointless.

outline.heading: Trivial questions amid real crises
outline.gist: He now declines Q&A questions that do not rank among the first hundred concerns while the community faces addiction, anxiety, depression, suicide attempts, apostasy and broken families; settling eight or twenty rakat of tarawih will not free anyone.

outline.heading: Preserve your own youth
outline.gist: Before reaching out to new Muslims, hold on to your own: half our children leave the masjid after high school and some fall into atheism and zina.

outline.heading: What 'the solution is Islam' should mean
outline.gist: He agrees with the slogan but asks what people mean by it. The answer is the basics, and Jumuah, the most basic of them, has become a chaotic circus used to draw people into institutions, with no leadership in it.

outline.heading: The hardest khutbahs he has given
outline.gist: His first seven or eight khutbahs after October 7 were the hardest of his life because he had no authority to offer next steps beyond silent protests and emails. He calls for a return to basics, which is why many recited this surah every Thursday night.

outline.heading: Outro

8:12.ar: إِذۡ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمۡ فَثَبِّتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۚ سَأُلۡقِي فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلرُّعۡبَ فَٱضۡرِبُواْ فَوۡقَ ٱلۡأَعۡنَاقِ وَٱضۡرِبُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ كُلَّ بَنَانࣲ‏
8:12.en: When thy Lord inspired the angels, (saying): I am with you. So make those who believe stand firm. I will throw fear into the hearts of those who disbelieve. Then smite the necks and smite of them each finger

8:13.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ شَآقُّواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥۚ وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
8:13.en: That is because they opposed Allah and His messenger. Whoso opposeth Allah and His messenger, (for him) lo! Allah is severe in punishment

8:20.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَلَا تَوَلَّوۡاْ عَنۡهُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَسۡمَعُونَ
8:20.en: O ye who believe! Obey Allah and His messenger, and turn not away from him when ye hear (him speak)

8:21.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَهُمۡ لَا يَسۡمَعُونَ
8:21.en: Be not as those who say, we hear, and they hear not

8:24.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمۡ لِمَا يُحۡيِيكُمۡۖ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيۡنَ ٱلۡمَرۡءِ وَقَلۡبِهِۦ وَأَنَّهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
8:24.en: O ye who believe! Obey Allah, and the messenger when He calleth you to that which quickeneth you, and know that Allah cometh in between the man and his own heart, and that He it is unto Whom ye will be gathered

8:25.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتۡنَةࣰ لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنكُمۡ خَآصَّةࣰۖ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
8:25.en: And guard yourselves against a chastisement which cannot fall exclusively on those of you who are wrong-doers, and know that Allah is severe in punishment

39:73.en: And those who keep their duty to their Lord are driven unto the Garden in troops till, when they reach it, and the gates thereof are opened, and the warders thereof say unto them: Peace be unto you! Ye are good, so enter ye (the Garden of delight), to dwell therein

Z1GXu4k9XKg.title: The Laws of Success and Victory 7: Adherence
Z1GXu4k9XKg.one_line: The law of adherence in Al-Anfal: obey Allah truly, because each person's sins weaken the whole ummah and can bring a trial that strikes everyone.
Z1GXu4k9XKg.summary: The seventh law, repeated throughout Al-Anfal, is adherence: following Allah's guidance exactly as taught, since hope only exists when we are doing what He asks. At Badr Allah gave a rare explicit reason for the enemy's defeat, their defiance of Him and His Messenger. He contrasts hearing with listening: believers are told not to be like those who say they heard but did not let it shape them. The call to respond to Allah and the Messenger is personal, with each person responding by capacity, and everything Allah calls to brings life, while He watches how each heart processes the command. Then comes the warning of a trial that does not strike only the wrongdoers. Using Zaynab's question to the Prophet, he argues that Muslims sail or sink together: personal sins are never free, because they weaken the ummah, so people should leave sin for the sake of their nation as well as their own souls. He cites Anas's complaint that later people took lightly what the companions counted as ruinous, Malik's warning to the young Shafi'i, and the story of Musa's rain prayer held back by one secret sinner until he repented. Every small daily choice ripples outward, and 'obey' is a command on which Allah's promise depends.

outline.heading: Opening
The law of adherence: hope requires doing what He teaches
outline.gist: The law repeated from the start of Al-Anfal to its end is adherence: unless we follow Allah's teaching exactly as He guided, we cannot hope for change, since hope only exists when you are doing something in keeping with it.

outline.heading: Why Badr's enemy fell: defiance of Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: Strike above the shoulders and at the fingertips points to their mistakes in big decisions and daily choices; rarely does the Quran give a reason, but here it does. Adherence runs both ways: not following brings a collective punishment, seen or unseen.

outline.heading: Hearing is not listening
outline.gist: Do not be like those who say they heard but did not: listening means letting what you hear enter the subconscious and drive behaviour. The surah reinforces this because nothing changes until each person holds himself accountable for his adherence.

outline.heading: Respond: each by capacity
outline.gist: 'Respond' is personal, shaped by each person's skills, reach, stage of life and struggles; the response to Allah differs from the response to His Messenger, but both must be the best you can give.

outline.heading: Everything He calls you to gives life
outline.gist: The 'idha' here is better read as 'when' than 'if': there is no circumstance in which Allah calls you to loss or weakness.

outline.heading: He stands between a person and his heart
outline.gist: Allah watches how your heart processes the command: the sincerity, intensity and genuineness with which you accept it.

outline.heading: A trial that strikes more than the wrongdoers
outline.gist: Fitnah can mean test, trial or a general calamity that shakes faith, which is why it is worse than killing; the next verse warns of one that will not fall only on the oppressors.

outline.heading: Zaynab's question
outline.gist: When the Prophet described a calamity that would take everyone, Zaynab asked whether they would be destroyed while righteous people were among them; yes, if those walking against Allah's teaching become many.

outline.heading: We sail or sink together
outline.gist: Muslims even enter Paradise in groups; only a rare prophet rejected by his nation comes alone, and for a Muslim calling for reform it is almost impossible to stand with no one.

outline.heading: Your sins are not free
outline.gist: An established principle of Islamic law: disobedience is one reason the ummah struggles. Your good deeds are channelled into its success and your bad deeds against it, affecting your children, family and nation.

outline.heading: Anas: what we counted as ruinous
outline.gist: Anas told later generations that deeds they thought trivial were counted in the Prophet's time among those that bring ruin, lamenting a decline in self-accountability.

outline.heading: Malik's warning to the young Shafi'i
outline.gist: Malik saw the boy's potential, as we should see our children's, and told him not to put out the light Allah placed in his heart with the darkness of sin; al-Shafi'i repeated it in his poetry all his life.

outline.heading: Interlude
Leave sin for your ummah as well
outline.gist: Good deeds strengthen the ummah and sins weaken it, so we all bear responsibility for what we see; leave sin to fix your relationship with Allah and also so the suffering we witness need not continue.

outline.heading: Calamity comes through sin and lifts through repentance
outline.gist: A saying found in nearly every book of spiritual wayfaring, of unknown origin; it works on a mystical and a practical level. A fitnah makes even those who did not cause it suffer, because they did not prevent it.

outline.heading: Musa's rain prayer and the hidden sinner
outline.gist: In the wilderness years, Musa's prayer for rain went unanswered because one man had disobeyed for forty years; torn between exposing himself and leaving everyone thirsty, he quietly repented, and the rain came.

outline.heading: Allah refuses to expose the one who returns
outline.gist: Musa asked who the man was; Allah said He had concealed him for forty years and would not expose him on the day he came back. The story is symbolic, and its symbolism is the point.

outline.heading: Every choice ripples, so obey
outline.gist: Like the butterfly effect and the time traveller's rule, every small act has weight; besides advocacy and long-term planning, daily choices strengthen or weaken the ummah. 'Obey' is a command, not a suggestion, and the promise depends on it.

outline.heading: Outro

Obey Allah and His Messenger and do not be like those who say 'we heard' but do not hear.
Respond to Allah and the Messenger when called to what gives you life; Allah comes between a person and his heart.
Beware a trial that will not strike only the wrongdoers among you.
Fitnah is worse than killing, because it can destroy many.

39:36.ar: أَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبۡدَهُۥۖ وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦۚ وَمَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنۡ هَادࣲ‏
39:36.en: Will not Allah defend His slave? Yet they would frighten thee with those beside Him. He whom Allah sendeth astray, for him there is no guide

39:37.ar: وَمَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّضِلٍّۗ أَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِعَزِيزࣲ ذِي ٱنتِقَامࣲ‏
39:37.en: And he whom Allah guideth, for him there can be no misleader. Is not Allah Mighty, Able to Requite (the wrong)

39:38.ar: وَلَئِن سَأَلۡتَهُم مَّنۡ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلۡ أَفَرَءَيۡتُم مَّا تَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِنۡ أَرَادَنِيَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ هَلۡ هُنَّ كَٰشِفَٰتُ ضُرِّهِۦٓ أَوۡ أَرَادَنِي بِرَحۡمَةٍ هَلۡ هُنَّ مُمۡسِكَٰتُ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ قُلۡ حَسۡبِيَ ٱللَّهُۖ عَلَيۡهِ يَتَوَكَّلُ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلُونَ
39:38.en: And verily, if thou shouldst ask them: Who created the heavens and the earth? they will say: Allah. Say: Bethink you then of those ye worship beside Allah, if Allah willed some hurt for me, could they remove from me His hurt; or if He willed some mercy for me, could they restrain His mercy? Say: Allah is my all. In Him do (all) the trusting put their trust

39:39.ar: قُلۡ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمۡ إِنِّي عَٰمِلࣱۖ فَسَوۡفَ تَعۡلَمُونَ
39:39.en: Say: O my people! Act in your manner. Lo! I (too) am acting. Thus ye will come to know

39:40.ar: مَن يَأۡتِيهِ عَذَابࣱ يُخۡزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيۡهِ عَذَابࣱ مُّقِيمٌ
39:40.en: Who it is unto whom cometh a doom that will abase him, and on whom there falleth everlasting doom

33:14.ar: وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأٓتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:14.en: If the enemy had entered from all sides and they had been exhorted to treachery, they would have committed it, and would have hesitated thereupon but little

34:36.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
34:36.en: Say (O Muhammad): Lo! my Lord enlargeth the provision for whom He will and narroweth it (for whom He will). But most of mankind know not

40:77.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۚ فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمۡ أَوۡ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيۡنَا يُرۡجَعُونَ
40:77.en: Then have patience (O Muhammad). Lo! the promise of Allah is true. And whether we let thee see a part of that which We promise them, or (whether) We cause thee to die, still unto Us they will be brought back

39:3.ar: أَلَا لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡخَالِصُۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ مَا نَعۡبُدُهُمۡ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلۡفَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فِي مَا هُمۡ فِيهِ يَخۡتَلِفُونَۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهۡدِي مَنۡ هُوَ كَٰذِبࣱ كَفَّارࣱ‏
39:3.en: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate

21:23.ar: لَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفۡعَلُ وَهُمۡ يُسۡـَٔلُونَ
21:23.en: He will not be questioned as to that which He doeth, but they will be questioned

pcejQPyB3Vc.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Az-Zumar (39:36-40)
pcejQPyB3Vc.one_line: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Fear of idols and superstition, decree and responsibility, guidance without compulsion, and tawakkul that leads to work.
pcejQPyB3Vc.summary: Verse 36 answers Quraysh, who warned the Prophet that their idols would harm him, as people warned Khalid before he destroyed al-'Uzza. Humans fear such things easily, and after centuries of ignorance, colonialism and dictatorship, belief in magic and the evil eye fills Muslim homes without evidence. Benefit and harm come only by Allah's decree, as the Prophet taught Ibn Abbas, so fearing people means imagining they can reach you beyond it, though one must still take precautions. He distinguishes qada, what you cannot affect and answer only with patience or gratitude, from qadar, what results from your effort and for which you are accountable. Allah guides and misguides by drawing near or distancing, as reward or punishment, never by compulsion, which would be injustice; He need only open a little of the world before someone. The sincere admit they were guided only because Allah arranged their circumstances, as Bilal refused to boast of his days with the Prophet. Allah is 'Aziz, beyond our grasp, which is why we cannot explain Abu Talib, and He avenges harm. Understanding decree makes tawakkul possible, and tawakkul bears fruit in work: do the good within reach where Allah placed you instead of cursing politicians.

outline.heading: Die thinking well of Allah
outline.gist: Days before his death the Prophet taught that none should die except with good thoughts of Allah; do not wait until the end to prepare.

outline.heading: Interlude
Az-Zumar turns sincerity from angle to angle
outline.gist: The surah closes the axis on obedience with obedience of the mind, seen in the heart and then the limbs.

outline.heading: Verse 36 recited, and the kasras of 'yudlil'
outline.gist: When a doubled letter is made jussive the two lams separate, and both take kasra to avoid two consecutive sukuns.

outline.heading: Sincerity keeps inner truthfulness alive
outline.gist: Whoever comes to Allah truthfully is saved even if after purification; sincerity means never lying to yourself or inflating or belittling yourself.

outline.heading: Threatened with their idols
outline.gist: The Prophet never insulted their gods but called them stones; Quraysh warned him of their harm.

outline.heading: Khalid destroys al-'Uzza
outline.gist: Warned of its power, Khalid destroyed it and came back to the Prophet for reassurance; humans naturally fear such things.

outline.heading: People certain they are bewitched
outline.gist: People ask about ruqyah water, insisting they are under magic; reading Quran over water is fine, but the certainty is not grounded.

outline.heading: How superstition spread among Muslims
outline.gist: Late Ottoman ignorance, colonialism and dictatorship let fortune tellers thrive; sorcery, envy, the evil eye and jinn became daily talk with no evidence.

outline.heading: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant?
outline.gist: Kafi means He protects and spares His servant; nothing besides Him is equal to Him.

outline.heading: Harm and benefit come only by His decree
outline.gist: Allah sends good and harm through people and events; the nation cannot benefit or harm you beyond what He wrote, as he taught Ibn Abbas.

outline.heading: Fear without giving up precautions
outline.gist: Fearing them assumes they can harm you beyond His decree; still get checked early and beware of traitors.

outline.heading: Qada and qadar defined
outline.gist: Qada is what you cannot affect, against the direction you were working; qadar is what follows from your effort, both expressing His eternal will.

outline.heading: The car at sixty or at a hundred
outline.gist: Hitting someone who jumps out while driving carefully is qada; hitting him while speeding and texting is qadar you answer for.

outline.heading: Lung cancer: decree and responsibility
outline.gist: The non-smoker's cancer and the smoker spared are both qada; the smoker owes extra gratitude for being spared.

outline.heading: Guidance and misguidance are not compulsion
outline.gist: Allah guides by directing and drawing near and misguides by distancing, often as reward or punishment.

outline.heading: Compulsion would be injustice
outline.gist: The companions did not debate this endlessly; failing a student who never sat the exam is unjust, so imagine attributing it to Allah.

outline.heading: The righteous watched for trials
outline.gist: When trials stopped they feared they were being lured by worldly ease; a trial means He is still bringing you back.

outline.heading: He need only scatter a little world in your path
outline.gist: Misguiding needs no force; He withholds provision from some knowing wealth would make them forget Him.

outline.heading: He knows your breaking point
outline.gist: As with those who would have given in had the enemy entered from every side, He protects by not testing beyond it.

outline.heading: You were guided because He arranged it
outline.gist: Your family, society and good friends were lined up by Allah; this is not fatalism but honesty about your small share, and it is sincerity.

outline.heading: Bilal: 'the truth got you married'
outline.gist: Proposing for his brother, Bilal stated only the shahadah and refused to boast of his days with the Prophet, which he saw as Allah's gift, not his achievement.

outline.heading: None can misguide whom Allah guides
outline.gist: You must call people but cannot decide who is guided; this relieves you, while you fear for your own state.

outline.heading: How easily one can leave the deen
outline.gist: Allah may give you what you sought for years and you go astray with it, or test you with what you cannot bear.

outline.heading: Al-'Aziz: beyond our grasp
outline.gist: 'Izzah is what cannot be reached; aspects of Allah's knowledge and aims lie beyond the mind.

outline.heading: Why did Abu Talib not believe?
outline.gist: He supported the Prophet more than most Muslims today; the reasons lie between Allah and His servant.

outline.heading: Possessor of retribution
outline.gist: Intiqam is repaying evil with evil; the Meccan verses never promised the Prophet he would not be harmed or live to see victory.

outline.heading: Harm only within His will
outline.gist: Whoever harms you does so within what Allah decreed, by his own choice, and Allah repays him; sincerity needs this understanding.

outline.heading: Verses 38-40 recited
outline.gist: They admit Allah created the heavens and earth; say Allah is sufficient for me; work according to your position.

outline.heading: Can their idols lift harm He wills?
outline.gist: Pagan Arabs knew Allah created all, yet claimed idols brought them near; even they could not claim an idol stops His harm.

outline.heading: Superstition as a tool of control
outline.gist: Such myths spread when knowledge is absent and are used by tyrants and the powerful to frighten people.

outline.heading: Allah is sufficient: understanding decree enables tawakkul
outline.gist: Tawakkul is a pillar of sincerity: give your effort, knowing outcomes are His.

outline.heading: Work according to your position
outline.gist: The fruit of tawakkul is work: the Prophet says 'I am working'; each will see his end in this world and the next.

outline.heading: Two errors: waiting and chasing mirages
outline.gist: The fatalist sits waiting and is held to account for it; the one who thinks things move without Allah exhausts himself chasing a mirage.

outline.heading: Work where Allah placed you
outline.gist: Many circumstances of your birth and life were never your choice; do the good within your reach and avoid the evil until you meet Him.

outline.heading: Change your small corner
outline.gist: The world is full of injustice and racism you cannot change; make the small change possible around you.

outline.heading: Cursing politicians is not sincerity
outline.gist: Abusing traitors and tyrants vents anger and sheds responsibility; the sincere ask Allah where their own work lies.

outline.heading: Outro

14:48.ar: يَوۡمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُۖ وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
14:48.en: On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens (also will be changed) and they will come forth unto Allah, the One, the Almighty

40:16.ar: يَوۡمَ هُم بَٰرِزُونَۖ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِنۡهُمۡ شَيۡءࣱۚ لِّمَنِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
40:16.en: The day when they come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. Whose is the Sovereignty this day? It is Allah's, the One, the Almighty

12:39.ar: يَٰصَٰحِبَيِ ٱلسِّجۡنِ ءَأَرۡبَابࣱ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيۡرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
12:39.en: O my fellow-prisoners! Are divers lords better, or Allah the One, Almighty

39:4.ar: لَّوۡ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدࣰ ا لَّٱصۡطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥۖ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
39:4.en: If Allah had willed to choose a son, He could have chosen what He would of that which He hath created. Be He Glorified! He is Allah, the One, the Absolute

38:65.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مُنذِرࣱۖ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
38:65.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I am only a warner, and there is no Allah save Allah, the One, the Absolute

13:16.ar: قُلۡ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلۡ أَفَٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرࣰّ اۚ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُ أَمۡ هَلۡ تَسۡتَوِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتُ وَٱلنُّورُۗ أَمۡ جَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلۡقِهِۦ فَتَشَٰبَهَ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّٰرُ
13:16.en: Say (O Muhammad): Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Take ye then (others) beside Him for protectors, which, even for themselves, have neither benefit nor hurt? Say: Is the blind man equal to the seer, or is darkness equal to light? Or assign they unto Allah partners who created the like of His creation so that the creation (which they made and His creation) seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Almighty

41:11.ar: ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانࣱ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلۡأَرۡضِ ٱئۡتِيَا طَوۡعًا أَوۡ كَرۡهࣰ ا قَالَتَآ أَتَيۡنَا طَآئِعِينَ
41:11.en: Then turned He to the heaven when it was smoke, and said unto it and unto the earth: Come both of you, willingly or loth. They said: We come, obedient

6:103.ar: لَّا تُدۡرِكُهُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدۡرِكُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَۖ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:103.en: Vision comprehendeth Him not, but He comprehendeth (all) vision. He is the Subtile, the Aware

He said: Thou wilt not see Me, but gaze upon the mountain! If it stand still in its place, then thou wilt see Me. And when his Lord revealed (His) glory to the mountain He sent it crashing down. 39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ

21:23.ar: لَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا يَفۡعَلُ وَهُمۡ يُسۡـَٔلُونَ

tOt7L3uiKu4.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: The All-Subduer, Al-Qahhar
tOt7L3uiKu4.one_line: Al-Qahhar, the name no one can share: everything submits to Allah, our choice is only of timing, so revere Him, never subdue others, and subdue yourself.
tOt7L3uiKu4.summary: He presents Al-Qahhar as a name unlike any other, one meant to make each listener leave at least one sin. The root means to overpower and compel, and unlike names such as Karim or Rahim, no human can claim it even figuratively, which is why the Quran almost always pairs it with Al-Wahid. He walks through the verses where it appears: the Day the earth is replaced and all stand exposed, the call asking who owns sovereignty that Day, Yusuf reminding his prison mates that the warden is not the true compeller, and the Prophet told to say he is only a warner. He then shows the name in action: heaven and earth answering willingly, the army of the elephant destroyed by birds, the knife refusing to cut Ismail, the fire made cool for Ibrahim, and death overtaking everyone. All creation submits gladly except humans, and even our choice is only when we will worship, now or on the Day of Judgment. Submission has no meaning without a Subduer worth submitting to. He closes with three steps: revere Allah to the point that it stops you from sinning and silences the endless why-questions, never compel or mistreat anyone weaker than you, and if you must subdue anything, subdue your own self to His will.

outline.heading: Opening
A name to leave a sin by
outline.gist: He introduces a unique name with the goal that each person walks out having left one sin.

outline.heading: Meaning of Al-Qahhar
outline.gist: To overpower and compel something to your will; everything from the atom to the galaxy is subdued by Allah. Qahhar appears six times and Qahir twice.

outline.heading: The earth replaced and all exposed
outline.gist: On the Day the earth and heavens are substituted, everyone stands fully exposed before the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Why it is paired with Al-Wahid
outline.gist: Other names can be shared figuratively by people, but no one can claim to be qahhar, so the Quran links it to the One and Only.

outline.heading: To whom belongs sovereignty today
outline.gist: On the Day nothing is hidden, the question of who owns the kingdom is answered: Allah, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Yusuf in prison
outline.gist: Yusuf uses this name in prison because inmates feel the warden compels them; he reminds them that the true Qahhar is Allah.

outline.heading: Had He wanted a son
outline.gist: Allah needs no sequence of causes; had He willed to take a son He could choose anything, but He is far above that.

outline.heading: The Prophet is only a warner
outline.gist: The Prophet is told not to let people think he is powerful; refusing the message is refusing Allah. Allah is Creator of everything, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: You cannot outrun God
outline.gist: Those who refuse cannot beat or outsmart Him; He subdued soil into living beings, the air and the cosmos.

outline.heading: Heaven and earth come willingly
outline.gist: The smoky sky and the earth answered His command willingly; no eye can perceive Him, and Musa collapsed at a mountain witnessing His majesty.

outline.heading: The army of the elephant and the burning seas
outline.gist: Abraha's army was destroyed by birds and pebbles; the elements of water will be made to burn, showing that every element obeys Him.

outline.heading: The knife and the fire obey
outline.gist: The knife would not cut Ismail and the fire became cool and peaceful for Ibrahim, who called those days the best of his life.

outline.heading: Subdued by death
outline.gist: Everyone present will be gone within a century; His compelling comes with beauty, and all creation enjoys submitting to Him.

outline.heading: Everything prostrates except us
outline.gist: Sun, moon, trees and animals all submit willingly; humans alone were given a choice, or at least the illusion of one.

outline.heading: You want and I want
outline.gist: A narration in which Allah says: submit to what I want and I give you what you want; refuse and in the end you get only what I wanted.

outline.heading: We only choose the time of worship
outline.gist: We will all worship Allah with total sincerity; the only choice is whether we do it now or on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Submission needs a Subduer
outline.gist: Islam as submission is meaningless without Al-Qahhar; the rites of Hajj and Ibrahim's acceptance rest on 'because He said so'.

outline.heading: The minbar shook
outline.gist: The Prophet recited that the earth is in His grip on the Day, then listed His names until the minbar shook beneath him.

outline.heading: First: revere Him, a reverence without oppression
outline.gist: He is Subduer over His servants yet Wise and All-Aware, and He sends angels who take each soul without fail.

outline.heading: First: the name ends the why-questions
outline.gist: Questions about why rules exist end with His will; the ability to question and disobey is lent and will be withdrawn, when even our limbs testify against us.

outline.heading: First: the name stops you before sinning
outline.gist: Remember that your freedom to sin is a brief exemption of perhaps ninety years, after which you are compelled like everything else.

outline.heading: Second: never subdue anyone
outline.gist: Compelling others is not our attribute; never force or mistreat those who for a moment seem weaker than us.

outline.heading: Third: subdue yourself
outline.gist: The one permitted use of the name is to overpower your own nafs and refuse to negotiate when it wants what is haram.

outline.heading: The illusion of choice will end
outline.gist: He restates the three steps and warns that one day we will be fully compelled and regret whom we sinned against.

5:27.ar: ۞وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱبۡنَيۡ ءَادَمَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ إِذۡ قَرَّبَا قُرۡبَانࣰ ا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنۡ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمۡ يُتَقَبَّلۡ مِنَ ٱلۡأٓخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقۡتُلَنَّكَۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
5:27.en: But recite unto them with truth the tale of the two sons of Adam, how they offered each a sacrifice, and it was accepted from the one of them and it was not accepted from the other. (The one) said: I will surely kill thee. (The other) answered: Allah accepteth only from those who ward off (evil)

5:28.ar: لَئِنۢ بَسَطتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقۡتُلَنِي مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطࣲ يَدِيَ إِلَيۡكَ لِأَقۡتُلَكَۖ إِنِّيٓ أَخَافُ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
5:28.en: Even if thou stretch out thy hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against thee to kill thee, lo! I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

5:29.ar: إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثۡمِي وَإِثۡمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلنَّارِۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَٰٓؤُاْ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
5:29.en: Lo! I would rather thou shouldst bear the punishment of the sin against me and thine own sin and become one of the owners of the fire. That is the reward of evil-doers

5:30.ar: فَطَوَّعَتۡ لَهُۥ نَفۡسُهُۥ قَتۡلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ فَأَصۡبَحَ مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
5:30.en: But (the other's) mind imposed on him the killing of his brother, so he slew him and became one of the losers

5:31.ar: فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابࣰ ا يَبۡحَثُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُرِيَهُۥ كَيۡفَ يُوَٰرِي سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيهِۚ قَالَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَىٰٓ أَعَجَزۡتُ أَنۡ أَكُونَ مِثۡلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡغُرَابِ فَأُوَٰرِيَ سَوۡءَةَ أَخِيۖ فَأَصۡبَحَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰدِمِينَ
5:31.en: Then Allah sent a raven scratching up the ground, to show him how to hide his brother's naked corpse. He said: Woe unto me! Am I not able to be as this raven and so hide my brother's naked corpse? And he became repentant

5:32.ar: مِنۡ أَجۡلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبۡنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفۡسَۢا بِغَيۡرِ نَفۡسٍ أَوۡ فَسَادࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمَنۡ أَحۡيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحۡيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعࣰ اۚ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُم بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَمُسۡرِفُونَ
5:32.en: For that cause We decreed for the Children of Israel that whosoever killeth a human being for other than manslaughter or corruption in the earth, it shall be as if he had killed all mankind, and whoso saveth the life of one, it shall be as if he had saved the life of all mankind. z2pafp56Xpg.title: Quranic Stories: Qabil and Habil (Cain and Abel)
z2pafp56Xpg.one_line: The first murder told in six scenes: accepted offerings and taqwa, refusing to shed a brother's blood, the nafs's slow persuasion, the crow, and envy.
z2pafp56Xpg.summary: The sheikh places the story of Adam's two sons in Surat al-Ma'idah, the surah of contracts, where it illustrates the sanctity of life, one of the five preservations, and Islam's fit with human nature. He tells it in six scenes. In the offering, Allah accepts only from the God-conscious; Habil gave his best while Qabil held back, and since Allah needs nothing, the offering is purely about intention. In the dispute, Habil refuses to raise his hand against his brother; the sheikh stresses the family dimension, the hadith on kinship hanging from the Throne, and Adam's grief. He links this to the Prophet's teaching to be the one killed rather than the killer in civil strife, told through Uthman's refusal to let any blood be spilt in Madinah during the siege, which he contrasts with the ruler who burned Syria to keep his seat. In the murder scene, the nafs gradually bends the will until a terrible idea feels like one's own. A crow, a creature a farmer despised, teaches Qabil to bury his brother, and his regret is about poor planning, not repentance. The following verse makes one unjust killing like killing all humanity. He ends by naming envy as the motive and warns that envy and faith cannot coexist in one heart.

outline.heading: A story shared across traditions
outline.gist: Versions appear beyond the Abrahamic scriptures, in texts of Central Asia and the Far East.

outline.heading: Why it sits in Surat al-Ma'idah
outline.gist: Among a run of core commands, the surah of contracts tells this story to show what keeping the contract means.

outline.heading: Divine rulings fit human nature
outline.gist: Commands protect our nature and others, which is why the five preservations recur across scriptures.

outline.heading: Sanctity of life and the six scenes
outline.gist: The Quran tells it in six scenes: offering, dispute, murder, crow, regret and burial.

outline.heading: Recite their news in truth
outline.gist: The story is told truthfully and revolves around haqq, a person's right to live.

outline.heading: Using Israelite reports for background
outline.gist: Scholars may borrow context from earlier scriptures when it creates no theological conflict, such as Adam's children born in twin pairs.

outline.heading: The marriage detail does not matter
outline.gist: He cannot verify the twin-marriage dispute and sets it aside as clutter that distracts from the story's point.

outline.heading: Scene 1: the offering
outline.gist: Habil the shepherd offered his best animal; Qabil the farmer offered poor crops, and only Habil's was accepted.

outline.heading: Allah accepts only from the God-conscious
outline.gist: The particle innama means exclusively; taqwa is asking before every act whether it pleases Allah.

outline.heading: Give the best you have
outline.gist: Allah gains nothing from offerings, so their worth is in intention; give your best time, effort and emotion. The story is about the inner life.

outline.heading: Scene 2: the dispute
outline.gist: No murder had happened yet; Qabil declares his intention and Habil says he will not raise his hand, for he fears Allah.

outline.heading: Bearing both sins
outline.gist: Habil does not wish his brother in Hell; he states the consequence for an oppressor.

outline.heading: A murder within the family
outline.gist: This was a tight-knit family and a premeditated decision, not a moment of anger.

outline.heading: Kinship hangs from the Throne
outline.gist: Allah keeps ties with whoever keeps kinship and cuts whoever cuts it, so Qabil was breaking both the law and the bonds of family.

outline.heading: The grief of Adam and Hawwa
outline.gist: Reflect on parents watching one child plan to kill another and losing both; Iblis was fulfilling his vow to mislead Adam's descendants.

outline.heading: Be the one killed, not the killer
outline.gist: In civil strife the one who sits is better than the one who stands; if forced, be Allah's slave who is killed.

outline.heading: Uthman's empire and its fitnah
outline.gist: Uthman ruled the largest empire of his day, and rapid expansion brought new peoples, cultures and unrest.

outline.heading: The siege of Uthman's house
outline.gist: Rebels besieged him while Madinah was emptied for Hajj; he ordered his defenders to stand down and refused to flee or let blood be shed.

outline.heading: Persevering as the Prophet foretold
outline.gist: He reminded the rebels of his record and held to the Prophet's prophecy that he must be patient through a trial.

outline.heading: The dream and his martyrdom
outline.gist: He dreamt the Prophet invited him to break his fast with him, and was killed the next day reciting the Quran.

outline.heading: Two kinds of ruler
outline.gist: Uthman chose death over bloodshed, while the ruler of Syria burned the country to keep his seat.

outline.heading: Scene 3: the nafs bends him
outline.gist: Tatawwa'at describes slow, repeated pressure until something gives; the nafs makes Shaytan's idea feel like your own decision.

outline.heading: Scene 4: the crow
outline.gist: Not knowing what to do with a human corpse, he watched a crow bury another crow.

outline.heading: Taught by a creature he despised
outline.gist: A farmer who hated crows had to learn from one, a lesson meant to humble him and show how little he knew.

outline.heading: Scene 5: regret without repentance
outline.gist: He regretted his poor planning, not the murder, and never went to his parents or sought forgiveness.

outline.heading: Killing one is killing all
outline.gist: All lives are equal in value, so unjustly taking one is like killing humanity and saving one is like saving all.

outline.heading: Habil was stronger and chose not to fight
outline.gist: Reports say Habil could have overpowered his brother but would not be the one to shed blood.

outline.heading: Envy drove it all
outline.gist: Envy at the accepted offering was the motive; faith and envy cannot share a heart, and envy leads to real harm.

8:45.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا لَقِيتُمۡ فِئَةࣰ فَٱثۡبُتُواْ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
8:45.en: O ye who believe! When ye meet an army, hold firm and think of Allah much, that ye may be successful

8:47.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ خَرَجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بَطَرࣰ ا وَرِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطࣱ‏
8:47.en: Be not as those who came forth from their dwellings boastfully and to be seen of men, and debar (men) from the way of Allah, while Allah is surrounding all they do

8:29.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِن تَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ فُرۡقَانࣰ ا وَيُكَفِّرۡ عَنكُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
8:29.en: O ye who believe! If ye keep your duty to Allah, He will give you discrimination (between right and wrong) and will rid you of your evil thoughts and deeds, and will forgive you. Allah is of Infinite Bounty

8:23.ar: وَلَوۡ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّأَسۡمَعَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ أَسۡمَعَهُمۡ لَتَوَلَّواْ وَّهُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ
8:23.en: Had Allah known of any good in them He would have made them hear, but had He made them hear they would have turned away, averse

8:70.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّمَن فِيٓ أَيۡدِيكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَسۡرَىٰٓ إِن يَعۡلَمِ ٱللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣰ ا يُؤۡتِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّمَّآ أُخِذَ مِنكُمۡ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
8:70.en: O Prophet! Say unto those captives who are in your hands: If Allah knoweth any good in your hearts He will give you better than that which hath been taken from you, and will forgive you. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

8:1.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَنفَالِۖ قُلِ ٱلۡأَنفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَصۡلِحُواْ ذَاتَ بَيۡنِكُمۡۖ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
8:1.en: They ask thee (O Muhammad) of the spoils of war. Say: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the messenger, so keep your duty to Allah, and adjust the matter of your difference, and obey Allah and His messenger, if ye are (true) believers

8:33.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمۡ وَأَنتَ فِيهِمۡۚ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمۡ وَهُمۡ يَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ
8:33.en: But Allah would not punish them while thou wast with them, nor will He punish them while they seek forgiveness

3:123.ar: وَلَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِبَدۡرࣲ وَأَنتُمۡ أَذِلَّةࣱۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
3:123.en: Allah had already given you the victory at Badr, when ye were contemptible. So observe your duty to Allah in order that ye may be thankful

8:65.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡقِتَالِۚ إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمۡ عِشۡرُونَ صَٰبِرُونَ يَغۡلِبُواْ مِاْئَتَيۡنِۚ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُم مِّاْئَةࣱ يَغۡلِبُوٓاْ أَلۡفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ
8:65.en: O Prophet! Exhort the believers to fight. If there be of you twenty steadfast they shall overcome two hundred, and if there be of you a hundred (steadfast) they shall overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they (the disbelievers) are a folk without intelligence

8:66.ar: ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمۡ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمۡ ضَعۡفࣰ اۚ فَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُم مِّاْئَةࣱ صَابِرَةࣱ يَغۡلِبُواْ مِاْئَتَيۡنِۚ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمۡ أَلۡفࣱ يَغۡلِبُوٓاْ أَلۡفَيۡنِ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
8:66.en: Now hath Allah lightened your burden, for He knoweth that there is weakness in you. So if there be of you a steadfast hundred they shall overcome two hundred, and if there be of you a thousand (steadfast) they shall overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. Allah is with the steadfast
